clauses.text:
November 22, 1907.
When transfers or promotions are properly applied for and are otherwise per¬
missible, the Civil Service Commission is hereby authorized, in its discretion,
looking to the good of the public service only, to waive requirements for exam¬
ination and to substitute for such examination so waived such other tests of
fitness and capacity as the Commission may decide.
In each case where such waiver is made the reasons therefor shall be stated
at length by the Commission and made matter of record in its minutes.
This order was recommended by the Commission for the reason that it was
believed that the service would be benefited if the discretion of waiving ex¬
aminations in certain cases of transfer or promotion, where such examinations
would ordinarily be required by the rules, should be placed in the hands of the
Commission.

648950Executive Order 1266 — Authorizing Civil Service Commission to Except Certain Unusual Positions from Examination1910President of the United States

The Civil Service Commission is hereby authorized to except from competitive examination, as contemplated by the civil-service act, section 2, clause Second, subject to the limitations prescribed by the statute and those now set forth in Rule II, certain positions arising, of unusual character, as to duties, and for which qualified persons are so rare that, in the judgment of the commission, they can not, in the interests of good civil-service administration, be filled through open competitive examination. In every instance of the exercise of this power the same procedure shall be followed as required in the Executive order of November 22, 1907.

Wm. H. Taft.

The White House,

December 1, 1910.
